filename: New-generation geostationary satellite reveals widespread midday depression in dryland photosynthesis during 2020 western U.S. heatwave.pdf
title: New-generation geostationary satellite reveals widespread midday depression in dryland photosynthesis during 2020 western U.S. heatwave
processes: Stomatal conductance response to heat and water stress
testbed_rationale: This study develops an empirical remote sensing retrieval model (Cubist regression tree) to map diurnal gross primary production, rather than providing an Earth system model parameterization or physical modeling testbed.
pain_points: Cloud contamination causes missing satellite land surface temperature observations, requiring gap-filling with reanalysis data (ERA5-Land).
Spatial scale mismatch between eddy covariance tower footprints and satellite or reanalysis grid cell resolutions.

Conventional diurnal upscaling from polar-orbiting satellite snapshots assumes radiation-symmetric diurnal cycles, introducing major biases during heatwaves and droughts where midday depression occurs.
extraction_notes: The Cubist regression model is used to map diurnal gross primary production across the CONUS at sub-daily resolution. It is a statistical remote sensing retrieval/upscaling method rather than a physics-based parameterization.
